derivations.claim: The matrices $\rho_n^{(0)}$ and $\rho_n^{(1)}$ are self-adjoint for every $n$. For every $z=(z_0,z_1)\in\mathbb C^2$, $\langle \rho_n^{(0)}z,z\rangle=(|z_0|^2+|z_1|^2)/2\ge0$ and $\langle \rho_n^{(1)}z,z\rangle=|z_0|^2\ge0$; each diagonal trace is one. Hence both matrices are density operators by [F3]–[F4]. Since the input factor is one-dimensional, its partial trace has one summand and returns the same matrix in each sequence at every $n$ by [F2].

The index $n$ in [F1] is the regulator index within each named sequence; it is distinct from the comparison label $r$. The definition assigns the sequence at the fixed section $\Sigma$ and declares no ordered family of cuts $\Sigma_s$, no corresponding state family $\rho_{s,n}$, and no comparison inequality between different cuts. Thus the two sequences in [given] are not states related by a physical evolution.

For every $n$, the eigenvalues of $\rho_n^{(0)}$ are $1/2,1/2$, and those of $\rho_n^{(1)}$ are $1,0$. By [F5]–[F7], $\log1=0$ and $\log2>0$: $\exp(0)=1<2=\exp(\log2)$, so strict increase gives $0<\log2$. By [F8], $\exp(-\log2)=1/2$, and uniqueness in [F5] gives $\log(1/2)=-\log2$. Therefore [F2] yields $S_{\mathrm{out},n}^{(0)}=k_B\log2$ and $S_{\mathrm{out},n}^{(1)}=0$ for every $n$.

For every $n$, [F1] and [A1] give $S_{\mathrm{gen},n}^{(1)}[\Sigma]-S_{\mathrm{gen},n}^{(0)}[\Sigma]=S_{\mathrm{out},n}^{(1)}-S_{\mathrm{out},n}^{(0)}=-k_B\log2<0$, because $k_B>0$. Both generalized-entropy sequences are constant in $n$, so they converge finitely and their renormalized values satisfy the same strict inequality. It is only a comparison of the two model-data sequences in [given], not an asserted evolution or a counterexample to an independently specified physical inequality.

The comparison in step 3.1 has one fixed section and two independently specified state-data sequences; it has no cut parameter or physical ordering. Under the countable-choice premise [A2], [F9] gives a conditional area inequality only for its stated smooth classical null-cut family, while [F10] gives an entropy coefficient and free offset only on its selected stationary family. Neither supplier specifies the state family or an inequality for the outside entropy required to compare different cuts. Therefore these fixed-section assignments and the two restricted geometric results do not establish a monotonicity inequality across any physical cut family. Such a claim requires separately specified cut and state data and a proof of the corresponding inequality.
